documents.title: DNS Security Introduction and Requirements
documents.sourceFinding: DNSSEC authenticates public RRsets and denials, not confidentiality, availability, transport or DNS management authorization. Last-hop reliance requires resolver and channel trust; absent applicable anchor is selected indeterminate interpretation.

documents.title: DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC)
documents.sourceFinding: BCP203 document map requires reading later updates; its RFC8624 reference is historical after RFC9904. It is not a substitute for record/validation specifications.

documents.title: Clarifications and Implementation Notes for DNS Security (DNSSEC)
documents.sourceFinding: Respect zone cuts and DNAME in denial, check CNAME absence for NODATA and NS presence for no-DS. Unknown digest treated like unsupported DNSKEY algorithm. Accept any valid RRSIG/path; SEP is not gate. Query AD interest differs from DO; copy response DO but receivers ignore it. Recommend upstream CD1; cached CD0 SERVFAIL requires fresh CD1 query. NSEC RDATA names are not downcased for signing; RRSIG names are.

documents.title: DNS Terminology
documents.sourceFinding: Current terminology obsoletes RFC8499 and explicitly preserves differences between RFC4033 and4035 DNSSEC state definitions; selected worksheet interpretation must be stated, especially missing anchor versus authenticated insecure delegation.

documents.title: Resource Records for the DNS Security Extensions
documents.sourceFinding: Protocol3 and Zone flag are verification prerequisites; SEP is not. RRSIG labels reconstruct wildcard owner. Inception/expiration use RFC1982 serial arithmetic. Canonicalize only defined DNS-name fields, not opaque TXT; key tag is selector not unique key. Read verified errata and RFC6840/9077/9824 updates.

documents.title: Protocol Modifications for the DNS Security Extensions
documents.sourceFinding: Parent authenticates DS; matching child DNSKEY authenticates child DNSKEY set. Missing DS field requires parent query, not insecure inference. Validation requires all prerequisites and one usable path. Authenticated TTL <=min(received RR TTL,received RRSIG TTL,OriginalTTL,remaining signature). Recursive CD echo mandatory; authoritative CD clearing SHOULD. Authenticated cached data may justify AD despite CD1. Bogus checking-client response SERVFAIL; CD1 raw-data return distinct.

documents.title: DNS Security (DNSSEC) Hashed Authenticated Denial of Existence
documents.sourceFinding: NSEC3 needs matching closest-encloser hash, covering next closer and wildcard cover for NXDOMAIN; exact hash with absent queried type/CNAME for NODATA. Opt-Out does not assert all covered names absent; AD prohibited with next-closer Opt-Out closest-encloser proof. Zero iterations still initial hash. NSEC3PARAM is authority coordination, not validator proof substitute.

documents.title: Guidance for NSEC3 Parameter Settings
documents.sourceFinding: Prefer NSEC when NSEC3 features unnecessary; publisher MUST iterations0 and SHOULD empty salt. Validator can choose authenticated insecure handling, SERVFAIL or ignore >0. EDE27 SHOULD follow authenticated unsupported parameter and MUST NOT assert it for ignored unverified parameter.

documents.title: Negative Caching of DNS Queries (DNS NCACHE)
documents.sourceFinding: NXDOMAIN negative cache keyed name/class; NODATA name/type/class. SOA carries negative TTL=min(SOA TTL,MINIMUM). Never reuse at TTL0. Read RFC9077 for aggressive proof reuse and RFC9520 replacing optional failure caching.

documents.title: NXDOMAIN: There Really Is Nothing Underneath
documents.sourceFinding: NXDOMAIN cut SHOULD reuse denied subtree within negative TTL, with stated exceptions; cache valid pre-existing data may continue. CNAME/DNAME denial applies last target, not original query. RFC9824 compact DNSSEC responses are not broad NXDOMAIN cuts.

documents.title: Aggressive Use of DNSSEC-Validated Cache
documents.sourceFinding: Validated complete same-zone proofs/wildcards SHOULD synthesize; missing proof MUST fetch. Opt-Out covering proof cannot prove name absence for aggressive caching. Reuse bounded by effective TTL and signatures; section5.4 replaced by RFC9077.

documents.title: NSEC and NSEC3: TTLs and Aggressive Use
documents.sourceFinding: Returned NSEC/NSEC3 TTL MUST min(SOA TTL,SOA.MINIMUM), allowing transient incremental-signing inconsistency. Resolver maximum effective negative TTL10800 RECOMMENDED. Optional SOA-based clamping if SOA present/cached, not mandatory per-proof SOA dependency. Wildcard result bounded by proof TTL too.

documents.title: Compact Denial of Existence in DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: NXNAME128 only signed bitmap meta-type, not stored RR/RCODE. NSEC QNAME->leading-null-label successor with RRSIG,NSEC,NXNAME bitmap returns NODATA-shaped NOERROR unless optional CO restoration. ENT only RRSIG,NSEC; genuine NODATA actual types. Explicit NXNAME query MUST FORMERR and MUST NOT forward/iterate; optional EDE30. CO context per hop/cache, reset to NOERROR for DO1 CO0 client. Minimal proofs cannot broad-aggressively synthesize. NSEC3 alternative ownerhash+1 has no known advantage.

documents.title: Extended DNS Errors
documents.sourceFinding: EDE15 option contains INFO-CODE and optional human text; diagnostic can appear with any RCODE, is unsigned and does not override RCODE requirements. Forwarding diagnostics implementation-dependent; source attribution SHOULD be retained. Omission is not validation success or failure.

documents.title: Negative Caching of DNS Resolution Failures
documents.sourceFinding: At most2 retries plus original query per address/transport. Mandatory failure cache1..300seconds, suppress corresponding outgoing queries until expiry; SHOULD configurable minimum and backoff. Mandatory DNSSEC validation failure caching distinct from authenticated negative cache. Limit ancestor retry amplification too.

documents.title: Definition and Use of DNSSEC Negative Trust Anchors
documents.sourceFinding: NTA is explicit nonautomatic operator bypass, limited scope/duration, automatic expiry, SHOULD <=oneweek; precedence over positive anchor at same node. SHOULD flush scoped cache when removed; bypass does not repair signatures or produce secure result.

documents.title: Domain names - concepts and facilities
documents.sourceFinding: Authoritative zones, recursion, referrals, aliases and caching are distinct. Bound resolution work. Later RFC4592 corrects wildcard/ENT existence, RFC6604 final xNAME RCODE, RFC9471 glue requirements.

documents.title: Domain names - implementation and specification
documents.sourceFinding: DNS header flags/RCODE are message/service facts, not signatures. ID plus question correlates query/response, TCP uses2-byte length. RFC4035 supplies AD/CD and RFC7766 updates TCP requirements; RFC9619 limits standard-query QDCOUNT.

documents.title: Extension Mechanisms for DNS (EDNS(0))
documents.sourceFinding: OPT not cached; advertised UDP payload is receiver capability not path guarantee. If DNSSEC required, no unsafe no-EDNS fallback. Middleboxes must not delete/modify OPT.

documents.title: DNS Transport over TCP - Implementation Requirements
documents.sourceFinding: General-purpose DNS implementations MUST UDP and TCP; TCP normal initial alternative not obsolete fallback. Retry TC-complete data via correlated TCP; response uses received transport/connection; pipelined replies may reorder.

documents.title: DNS Proxy Implementation Guidelines
documents.sourceFinding: Transparent proxy should relay flags/unknown types/EDNS; must support TCP and must not clear TC. Forwarding route does not install DNSSEC anchor or turn transmitter into signer.

documents.title: Indicating Resolver Support of DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: DO requests auxiliary DNSSEC records, not validation on/off. Explicit DNSSEC-type query gets requested type even DO0. Recursive security-aware outbound DO1 regardless downstreamDO. Missing security data does not prove unsigned zone. Read current RFC4035/6840 over obsolete SIG/KEY/NXT examples.

documents.title: Specification for DNS over Transport Layer Security (TLS)
documents.sourceFinding: DoT defaultTCP853, TLS first,2-byte message length, match ID/question on same connection. Encryption protects hop privacy but not origin validity of DNS data. RFC8310 updates authenticated usage profiles.

documents.title: Usage Profiles for DNS over TLS and DNS over DTLS
documents.sourceFinding: Strict Privacy requires encrypted authenticated configured endpoint, no mid-query fallback to Opportunistic; trusted ADN/PKIX or pins required. Opportunistic may be unauthenticated or cleartext. Neither substitutes DNSSEC validation.

documents.title: DNAME Redirection in the DNS
documents.sourceFinding: Authenticate DNAME and verify substitution; synthesized CNAME need not own signature. Target independently validated; DNAME owner itself not redirected. Cache synthesis TTL follows DNAME with required compatibility for zero TTL.

documents.title: The Role of Wildcards in the Domain Name System
documents.sourceFinding: ENT exists. Closest encloser determines only wildcard source; no fallback wildcard search. Expanded conventional signature binds reconstructed wildcard owner and must prove no closer match.

documents.title: Minimally Covering NSEC Records and DNSSEC On-line Signing
documents.sourceFinding: Minimal NSEC online signing narrows denial ranges and entails online private signing custody; distinct from RFC9824 NXNAME/NODATA technique. Not broad traditional precomputed interval evidence.

documents.title: Cryptographic Algorithm Identifier Allocation for DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: Registration requires RFC, not necessarily Standards Track; registry listing is not mandatory implementation. Private253/254 retain own identifying data. Later9157/9904 refine registry policy.

documents.title: Applicability Statement: DNS Security (DNSSEC) DNSKEY Algorithm Implementation Status
documents.sourceFinding: Historical algorithm-implementation policy, obsoleted by8624, itself obsoleted by9904. Do not treat old table as current operator policy.

documents.title: Handling of Unknown DNS Resource Record (RR) Types
documents.sourceFinding: Preserve unknown/opaque RDATA bytes and case; only specified known domain-name fields canonicalized, and compression only where permitted. RFC6840 supplies modern NSEC/RRSIG clarification.

documents.title: Serial Number Arithmetic
documents.sourceFinding: Serial comparison wraps modulo2^32 and is undefined exactly half a range apart; do not compare RRSIG times as ordinary unbounded integers.

documents.title: Revised IANA Considerations for DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: Registry assignment criteria for DS/NSEC3 hash/flags, not permission to invent successful proof with unsupported parameters; updated by9904.

documents.title: xNAME RCODE and Status Bits Clarification
documents.sourceFinding: Final xNAME target lookup determines RCODE; AD covers all answer/relevant authority, AA tied first owner. A signed alias alone never blesses target.

documents.title: DNS Glue Requirements in Referral Responses
documents.sourceFinding: Referral all available in-domain glue or TC set if cannot fit; glue addresses remain routing data and not authenticated merely co-carried with DS.

documents.title: In the DNS, QDCOUNT Is (Usually) One
documents.sourceFinding: OPCODE0 question count must not exceed1; FORMERR on >1. Selected synthetic packets each contain exactly1 question.

documents.title: Domain Name System (DNS) Case Insensitivity Clarification
documents.sourceFinding: Only US-ASCII uppercase/lowercase DNS-label equivalence; case preservation and DNSSEC canonical transformation do not imply arbitrary text downcasing.

documents.title: Moving DNSSEC Lookaside Validation (DLV) to Historic Status
documents.sourceFinding: DLV mechanism Historic and RRtype obsolete; do not reintroduce DLV from RFC6840 historical appendix.

documents.title: Deprecating the Use of SHA-1 in DNSSEC Signature Algorithms
documents.sourceFinding: Internal source discrepancy preserved: section2 mandates operator alg5/7 unsupported/insecure while section5 registry Use-for-validation remains RECOMMENDED and implementation MUST; section4 says not changing those columns. Selected operator policy follows section2; no fabricated unified cell. Does not deprecate NSEC3 SHA1 hashing.

documents.title: Deprecate Usage of ECC-GOST within DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: Old ECC-GOST alg12 and digest3 prohibited/new creation; old validation paths treated unsupported/insecure; does not alter newer GOST2012 algorithms. Distinct from generic failed supported signature.

documents.title: Algorithm Implementation Requirements and Usage Guidance for DNSSEC
documents.sourceFinding: Historical algorithm table supersedes6944 but is superseded by9904; implementation and operator use must not be conflated.

documents.title: DNSSEC Cryptographic Algorithm Recommendation Update Process
documents.sourceFinding: Current framework has separate Use for Signing/Delegation, Use for Validation, Implement for Signing/Delegation, Implement for Validation columns. IANA snapshot and exact policy conflicts owned by publication shard; resolution uses13/DS2 and explicit supported capability list.
